\chapter{Right, Wrong, Sure}
\label{ch:hi-right-wrong-sure}
\hlchaptermodality{112}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say something is right or wrong, ask if someone is sure, react with really? and oh!}

Complete HI-C112-are: reactions and judgements.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[sahī]{\hi{सही} (sahī) — right, correct}

\label{lesson:HI-C112-sahi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for I could not hear it, then the Hindi for please write it down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{सही}}
\textbf{\hi{सही}} (\emph{sahī}) — \textquotedblleft{}right, correct\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{सही} \hi{जवाब}} — \textquotedblleft{}the right answer\textquotedblright{}. Said alone, \textbf{\hi{सही}!} agrees: \textquotedblleft{}right!\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A word for getting it right.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sahī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sahī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{sahī!}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for I could not hear it, then the Hindi for please write it down, then say \emph{sahī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{सही} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Right, correct\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ġalat]{\hi{ग़लत} (ġalat) — wrong, incorrect}

\label{lesson:HI-C112-galat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for please write it down, then the Hindi for right.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{ग़लत}}
\textbf{\hi{ग़लत}} (\emph{ġalat}) — \textquotedblleft{}wrong\textquotedblright{}.

The opposite of \textbf{\hi{सही}}. \textbf{\hi{यह} \hi{ग़लत} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}this is wrong\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Right and wrong, as a pair.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ġalat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ġalat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{yah ġalat hai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for please write it down, then the Hindi for right, then say \emph{ġalat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{ग़लत} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Wrong, incorrect\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[pakkā]{\hi{पक्का} (pakkā) — sure, certain; firm}

\label{lesson:HI-C112-pakka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for right, then the Hindi for wrong.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{पक्का}}
\textbf{\hi{पक्का}} (\emph{pakkā}) — \textquotedblleft{}sure, certain\textquotedblright{}, and of a thing, \textquotedblleft{}firm, ripe\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{पक्का}?} — \textquotedblleft{}for sure?\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\hi{पक्का}!} — \textquotedblleft{}definitely!\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A question and an answer in one word.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pakkā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pakkā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{pakkā?}, then answer \emph{pakkā!}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for right, then the Hindi for wrong, then say \emph{pakkā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{पक्का} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sure, certain; firm\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sac meṁ?]{\hi{सच} \hi{में}? (sac meṁ?) — really?}

\label{lesson:HI-C112-sachme}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for wrong, then the Hindi for sure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{सच} \hi{में}?}
\textbf{\hi{सच} \hi{में}?} (\emph{sac meṁ?}) — \textquotedblleft{}really?\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}in truth?\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{सच}} is the \textquotedblleft{}true\textquotedblright{} you know, with \textbf{\hi{में}}, \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A way to show surprise.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sac meṁ?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sac meṁ?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{sac meṁ?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for wrong, then the Hindi for sure, then say \emph{sac meṁ?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{सच} \hi{में}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Really?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[are]{\hi{अरे} (are) — oh!, hey!}

\label{lesson:HI-C112-are}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for sure, then the Hindi for really.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{अरे}}
\textbf{\hi{अरे}} (\emph{are}) — \textquotedblleft{}oh!\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}hey!\textquotedblright{}, a cry of surprise.

\textbf{\hi{अरे}, \hi{सच} \hi{में}?} — \textquotedblleft{}oh, really?\textquotedblright{}. It is informal: use it with friends.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Right, wrong, sure, really, oh: five reactions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{are}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{are}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{are, sac meṁ?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for sure, then the Hindi for really, then say \emph{are} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{अरे} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Oh!, hey!\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
